# ai-agent4j

> The core of llm4j: a lightweight ReAct agent library for Java 17, with no vendor SDKs (about 440 KB). It supports Gemini, Anthropic Claude, Sarvam and local Ollama models behind one contract. Agents are ordinary objects built with a builder: a client, tools, skills, memory, an approval callback and a budget.

Maven: `io.github.srijithunni7182:ai-agent4j:5.0`. This file covers the core library. For the whole stack (tools, Loom workflows, Engram, eval4j, security), see the [repository llms.txt](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/llms.txt).

## The agent

- `ReActAgent` runs a loop: the model writes a short `"plan"` (`"thought"` is still read), calls a `Tool`, reads the observation, and repeats until it gives a final answer or reaches `maxIterations` (default 10).
- The builder takes `llmClient`, `systemPrompt`, `addTool`/`addTools`, `addSkill(AgentSkill.fromClasspath(...))`, `persona`, `conversationHistory`, `semanticMemory`, `approvalCallback`, `auditLogger`, `biasMonitor`, `budget`, `maxTokensPerCall` and `onBudgetExhausted(RETURN_PARTIAL | FAIL | SUSPEND)`.
- `AgentResult` carries the final answer, each step (thought, action, observation), confidence, token usage and cost. `AgentEventListener` streams thoughts and tool calls (see Thought-Streaming).

## Providers

- `GoogleProvider`, `AnthropicProvider`, `SarvamChatProvider` and `OllamaProvider` implement one `LLMProvider` contract, with `chat` and streaming `chatStream`. The system prompt, finish reasons (the raw value is in `metadata.finish_reason_raw`) and errors mean the same on every provider.
- Typed exceptions, all `LLMException`:
  - `AuthenticationException`;
  - `InvalidRequestException`;
  - `RateLimitException`, carrying `RateLimitInfo.resetAt()`;
  - `ServiceUnavailableException`;
  - `ContentBlockedException`.
- `RoutingLLMClient` routes by cost, for example a fast model for easy steps and a stronger one for hard ones.

## Tools

- `Tool`: `getName`, `getDescription`, `execute(Map<String,Object>)`, and `requiresApproval(args)` to make a call wait for a person through `ApprovalCallback`. With no callback set, a call that needs approval is **blocked**.
- Built-ins: calculator, date and time, web search. `McpClient` and `McpToolAdapter` bring in tools from MCP servers; the OpenAPI tool turns a REST spec into tools.
- Effect contracts for tools that change the world:
  - `Effectful`: is this call a read or an effect?
  - `EffectJournal`: record effects so they are never repeated;
  - `ToolKind`.
- Ready-made, hardened tools (`webhook`, `email`, `http`, `file`, `shell`, read-only `sql`) are in the separate `ai-agent4j-tools` module.
- `DelegateTaskTool` (`delegate_task`): a manager agent builds a sub-agent on the fly with tools picked from a `ToolRegistry`. **The registry is the permission boundary**: register only what any sub-agent may hold. In Loom, prefer `delegate` to declared agents.

## Safety and control

- `Budget.builder().tokens(50_000).calls(40).cost("0.50").warnAt(0.8).window(Window.DAY).build()`: caps checked **before** each call. A call that can't be paid for throws `BudgetExceeded` without reaching the model.
- `BudgetedLLMClient` meters any client. `BudgetSet` applies several budgets per call. `PriceTable.load(path)` prices money budgets.
- HTTP 429s are parsed: the Gemini body (including daily quotas), Anthropic and OpenAI headers, and `Retry-After`. Short limits are waited out; long ones raise `RateLimitException` with the exact reset time.
- `MaskingLLMClient` with `PIIDetector` replaces emails, phone numbers, SSNs, card numbers and IP addresses with placeholders in every message sent to the model, tool results included.
- `BiasMonitor` (rules-based or judged by a model) flags sweeping statements about groups.
- `AuditLogger` records tool calls, approvals and detections, with personal data masked.

## Memory and knowledge

- `ConversationHistory`: short-term context. `SemanticMemoryService` and `SemanticMemoryConfig`: long-term fact recall.
- `InMemoryVectorStore` for development. `PGVectorStore`, Pinecone and local ONNX/DJL embeddings are in `ai-agent4j-addons`.
- RAG over documents, knowledge graphs, a prompt registry, Markdown skills and personas.

## Scheduling

- `AgentScheduler` and `ScheduledActionTool` schedule work in memory.
- For schedules that survive restarts, and runs that pause on limits and resume, use Loom: [Budgets, Pausing and Scheduling](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/BUDGETS_AND_SCHEDULING.md).
